---
title: "My Journey"
---

Helping people has always been a central part of who I am. I've been drawn to sociology for its ability to explain how social norms, values, and beliefs shape the way people and groups function within society. That interest gave me a strong foundation for understanding behavior, problem solving, and the human side of organizational work.

Over time, I gained experience in on-boarding, training, and performance evaluation through HR adjacent roles, which gave me practical insight into how organizations support and develop their people. Business school further expanded my understanding of the business side of that work, while also highlighting a gap I wanted to close: building stronger research and analytic skills.

My experience in contract roles over the past few years has shown me how much organizational structure and support can affect people's ability to do their best work. It also reinforced my desire to contribute in a more meaningful and informed way.

I'm now actively developing my research skills and learning R so I can move from working around data to working with it directly. This site is where I document that journey: the ideas, the challenges, and the progress as I build something more aligned with the kind of work I want to do.
